content: Accept clai2's Logfire MCP and PostHog auth under FastMCP 4's `httpx2` client

Connect `clai2`'s `logfire_mcp` and `posthog` plugins under FastMCP 4 Under FastMCP 4, `clai2` fails every turn while the `logfire_mcp` plugin is enabled: ``` RuntimeError: Client failed to connect: Invalid "auth" argument: ``` The `posthog` plugin fails the same way with `SavedKeyAuth` when it connects with a `/keys` entry. No issue was filed. This follows up on #9912, which fixed the shared MCP client factory and listed `DeviceAuth` and `SavedKeyAuth` as possibly affected but not reproduced. ### Cause `pydantic-ai-slim[mcp]` accepts `fastmcp-slim>=3.3.0,<5`. The workspace lock pins FastMCP 3, but a fresh `uvx`/`pip` resolve of `pydantic-clai2` gets `fastmcp-slim` 4.0.11 with MCP SDK 2.3.0, which run on `httpx2`. Since #9912, `pydantic_clai2.mcp.http_client` builds the MCP connection with the SDK's `create_mcp_http_client`, so under FastMCP 4 that is an `httpx2.AsyncClient`. `httpx2`'s `BaseClient._build_auth` accepts only an `httpx2.Auth` (or a tuple or a callable) and raises `TypeError: Invalid "auth" argument` for anything else. `DeviceAuth` and `SavedKeyAuth` subclass legacy `httpx.Auth`. (`SignIn` subclasses FastMCP's own `OAuth`, so it already follows the installed generation.) There is a second FastMCP 4 problem in `logfire_oauth`: the device flow (discovery, registration, polling, refresh) also used `http_client`, so under FastMCP 4 its errors are `httpx2` errors. Its `except httpx.HTTPError` / `except httpx.TransportError` handlers don't catch those. An unreachable Logfire then failed with a raw `httpx2.ConnectError: All connection attempts failed` instead of `Logfire sign-in failed: ConnectError. Run /logfire_mcp login to retry.`, and a failed refresh crashed the request instead of falling back to signing in again. ### Fix - `DeviceAuth` and `SavedKeyAuth` subclass both `httpx.Auth` and `httpx2.Auth`, so whichever client the installed FastMCP builds accepts them. Their flows touch only `request.headers` and `response.status_code`, which both generations share. Their overrides take either family's `Request` through a constrained `TypeVar`. A single `pyright: ignore` per class covers the one inherited flow method (`auth_flow` or `sync_auth_flow`) that the two bases declare for their own `Request` types. - The Logfire device flow builds its own legacy `httpx.AsyncClient`, with the MCP SDK's 30 s / 300 s read timeouts and no redirects, the same settings `http_client` gave it under FastMCP 3. Its error handling now matches the client it uses under both FastMCP versions. FastMCP 3 behavior is unchanged. **Why not cap `fastmcp-slim<4` for `clai2`?** `clai2` already supports FastMCP 4 deliberately. `pydantic_ai.mcp` (#8461) and `clai2`'s own `http_client` (#9912) were made to work on both generations, and no `clai2` or harness extra caps FastMCP except `harness[stackone]`. A cap would also roll back users whose other plugins work on FastMCP 4 today. **Why both bases, not one picked by FastMCP version?** That would need a version or type probe at import time. Pyright would then see only one base, and the class would still break whenever a client of the other family is used, for example in tests or with a user-supplied client. With both bases, the class is accepted by either client without detection. ### Not in this PR A failing optional MCP server (for example, `logfire_mcp` while Logfire is unreachable) still fails the whole turn. Making plugin-contributed MCP toolsets skip a server that fails to connect is a separate behavior change, and its right home (the plugin loader or a wrapper toolset) is a design question. It is not part of this fix. ### Verification - Reproduced with `fastmcp-slim` 4.0.11 and MCP 2.3.0 installed in a separate venv, connecting a real FastMCP `Client` over `StreamableHttpTransport(..., httpx_client_factory=http_client)`: - `DeviceAuth` on `main`: `Client failed to connect: Invalid "auth" argument`. On this branch: `Logfire sign-in failed: ConnectError. Run /logfire_mcp login to retry.`, the same as on FastMCP 3.4.7. - `SavedKeyAuth` on `main`: `Invalid "auth" argument`. On this branch: `PostHog has no key. ...`, the same as on FastMCP 3.4.7. - New regression tests (all three fail on `main` and pass here): - `test_logfire_oauth.py::TestDeviceAuth::test_fastmcp_4_connections_accept_it`: a real `httpx2.AsyncClient` with `DeviceAuth` sends the token, then gets a 401 and refreshes and retries once. - `test_logfire_oauth.py::TestDeviceAuth::test_sign_in_failures_are_reported_under_fastmcp_4`: with the SDK's client factory replaced by an `httpx2` one (as in FastMCP 4), an unreachable server still raises `SignInError`. - `test_posthog.py::test_fastmcp_4_connections_accept_saved_key_auth`: a real `httpx2.AsyncClient` with `SavedKeyAuth` sends the saved key. - `tests/clai2/test_logfire_oauth.py`, `test_posthog.py` and `test_logfire_mcp.py` pass. Ruff passes, and Pyright is clean on both changed source files. ### Checklist - [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md). - [x] Any permitted **compatibility impact** has a label, warning, migration, release note, and exact API-check waiver. - [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

**Verdict:** Not approved

Macroscope's review found this PR not approvable — This PR is a focused FastMCP 4 compatibility fix with targeted coverage, but it changes production OAuth and bearer-authentication request paths, including the client used for sign-in and token refresh. Authentication-sensitive runtime changes warrant human review.
